body.v: Your HelvetiCare online account needs a quick check after our system update. It takes one minute.
If you do not confirm, some services may be paused.

hotspots.explain: The display name says HelvetiCare, but helveticare-online.example is not the insurer's domain, helveticare.example.
Using your first name sounds personal, but scammers can find it easily. It does not prove who wrote the email.
"Some services may be paused" is a soft threat, so you act before thinking.
The text looks like helveticare.example, but the link really goes to helveticare-online.example. Text can say anything.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone using HelvetiCare's name. The display name and the greeting are right, but the address is on helveticare-online.example.
choices: Someone using a lookalike address and your first name
HelvetiCare, because it knows your name

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: A quiet fear of losing services, with a hint that it is quick and easy.
choices: A quiet fear of losing services
None: it is a routine notice

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Click the link and log in to 'confirm' your details, which would hand your login to the sender.
choices: Click the link and log in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open the HelvetiCare app, or type the insurer's address yourself, and see whether anything needs confirming.
choices: Click the link and check the page looks right
Reply to ask if it is genuine

actions.label: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself and look for any notice
actions.consequence: There is no notice. The email was fake.

actions.label: Click the link and log in, because it knows your name
actions.consequence: The page looks right, but your login goes straight to the scammer.

actions.label: Hover over the link and log in if the page looks right
actions.consequence: A lookalike page can look perfect. You gave your login to the scammer.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: Good call. You gave nothing away.

attacker_reveal: I used your name, the right logo and perfect language... and the link text lied. A name in the greeting is easy to find, so it never proves who is writing.
